items.evidence: Under "## The bottom line" the overview runs "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**" (the 553-volume count, the five ways corruption worked, the 29 documents), then "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" (the two channels, "not added together"), then "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" (a)–(e), followed by Scope and Decisions; "## Findings" comes only after all three.

Every figure carries its set: "About 2,200 of its roughly 311,000 ordinary documents (about one in 140, spread over about 400 volumes)"; "in a sample of forty, six were not about official corruption"; "29 documents from 20 volumes"; "only about one series in thirty-five among the 698 series their facts file describes begins before 1940"; "only four documents in the whole series, all from 1977–1980"; "I read 63 documents whole ... kept 29 of them, and quoted 17 passages". A scan finds no percent sign. One gap that fails nothing: the decade-by-decade comparison is said to have been made but its result is never given.

All 29 distinct documents are cited in the printed form with a link, e.g. "Foreign Relations of the United States, 1969–1976, Volume E–9, Part 2, Documents on the Middle East Region, 1973–1976, Document 122 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1969-76ve09p2/d122)" and "Foreign Relations of the United States, Diplomatic Papers, 1943, China, Document 202 (https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1943China/d202)"; 34 id tokens in the file, all 34 inside history.state.gov links. The one short form, in part 2, "(cited under the April 1960 Vietnam cable, Document 135 of the 1958–1960 Vietnam volume)", is a back-reference to a document given in full with its link in the Vietnam finding, neither a bare id pair nor a title alone. All 29 are in the collection.

Part 3(a): "I searched the root word and a family of related words (bribe, graft, embezzle, venal, kickback, malfeasance, nepotism) in the index, then spelled-out variants in the volumes' own text, with a word that cannot occur as a control and a common phrase as a check"; (c): "that exact phrase appears in only four documents in the whole series, all from 1977–1980"; the index is "all 553 volumes" (part 1 and Scope); the controls' results are in How this was done: "a nonsense word as a control that came back at zero and a common phrase as a control that appeared in every volume". Weaker than the other three overviews: the control phrase is unnamed and its figures sit in the method section rather than beside the claim; (d) says plainly that no full period-vocabulary search was run before 1940, a stated gap rather than a claimed zero.

A scan of the overview finds no percent sign, no SQL keyword, no underscore and no path-like string; its 34 frus id tokens are all inside history.state.gov links. Tools are named only descriptively: "the full-text index of all 553 volumes", "the similarity index", "the volumes' original markup", "their facts file".

judge:s1.rankingReason: s6: 30 documents in six findings, among them Koreagate, the one case where an allegation visibly changed what the executive asked of Congress, and Hawaii 1893; every cannot-get is a counted search with the control phrase and its figures beside it; decade rates given; the semantic neighbours' contribution explained. s2: 19 documents in six crisp findings with bulleted, fully cited quotations; controls named with figures beside each claim; decade rates, the duplicate count and an explicit inclusion rule stated. s1: 29 documents, a sound five-role answer and the best-built collection (section prose, a note on every document, 17 verified excerpts), but the decade comparison is described without its result, the control phrase is unnamed and its figures sit in the method section, and each finding ends in a run of appended citations that is hard to read. s7: 11 documents only; the 1875 Venezuela case is a real find and the controls are well stated, but the findings are thin, one lot is resolved only as "or possibly", and the overview twice sends the reader to the memo for its figures.

score:s1.notes: All four required files are present (memo.md, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), with 40 scripts and outputs beside them. Compliance 38 of 42 scoreable items (90.5%). Verification against the read-only index reproduced every SQL-backed figure I re-ran: the canary 553|321749|1103|8481, the denominator 311,429 in 551, the headline 2,175 in 399 (2,200 in 401 before Ed2), the four FCPA-phrase documents, the 1930s and 1960s decade rows, the document_sources and external_citations rows cited, and eight quotations as exact substrings of body_text; the bundled JSON confirms 62D26 -> NAID 1965953 / A1 3113, 71D461 -> 603208, 76D169 -> 2602428, 20 of 698 series-facts rows before 1940, Johnson NSF 567979 and the Carter WHCF Subject File 165203. The vector run was real: five digests agree, 553 shard headers match, both baselines are computed before any neighbour is read, and the two edition twins are masked. The four violations: V2 (decode shown, no known-pair spot check anywhere), V5 (the cluster figure is compared to the corpus unclustered share alone, by the memo's own admission), and O2/O2' (eight number-words in the overview have no trace row: five ways, two different things, the two discussed, two departing officers, four threats, second greatest, five groups, three things; the session's own statistics all trace). Two facts worth carrying forward: (1) the index and vector artifact hold a third Ed2 id, frus1977-80v09Ed2, whose first edition is absent from both, so it is not a twin and the session's two-volume mask gave the right result without ever checking for it; (2) the overview says "I read 63 documents whole" while memo M4.5 discloses the cited documents were read in KWIC windows and openings, "not necessarily every paragraph" — P4 is met by the explicit count, but the overview's wording overstates the memo's disclosure. V6 is not_applicable because no cosine was ever computed or shown (all similarity figures are Hamming distances); the memo names the offsets and labels its zero cosines raw, which engages the rule without exercising it, the same situation as E3. V7 was not scored, per the task.

refute:s1.fabricationDetails: None. I applied the guide's rule myself (refuter/quote_check.py: lower-case, drop everything but [a-z0-9], split at …, ... and [...], require every segment in order at increasing offsets in header||dateline||source_note||body_text of the exact pair). Overview.md holds 18 passages inside quotation marks attributed to a document: Q01 (frus1950v06/d832), Q03 (frus1961-63v23/d358), Q04 (frus1977-80v23/d252), Q06 and Q07 (frus1964-68v05/d258), Q08 (frus1964-68v05/d197, the nested-quote Thieu passage), Q10 (frus1969-76v06/d175), the inline fragment 'as a means of guarding U.S. interests.' plus Q13 and Q14 (frus1969-76ve09p2/d122), Q15 (frus1969-76v27/d45), Q17 (frus1977-80v18/d206), Q18 (frus1969-76ve11p1/d159), Q19 (frus1969-76ve09p2/d161), Q20 (frus1969-76ve12/d219), Q26 (frus1943China/d202), Q24 (frus1961-63v22/d244), Q25 (frus1961-63v22/d249): 18 of 18 pass, each a single segment (no ellipsis in any), and each is literally present in overview.md. The collection's 17 excerpts (the same 17 Q texts, each under its own document entry) pass 17 of 17. The two quoted fragments inside collection notes, 'in the Western sense' (d206) and 'standing firm' (d161), also pass; 'not from any moralistic concern' (d122 note) is a substring of Q13. A cross-check found each overview passage in no other row of document_cache, so none is a quotation lifted from a different document. The word "corrupt" in quotation marks in the bottom line is the search term (trace table -> M3.2), not a document quotation, and is not counted. The session's own verify_quotes.py (26 of 26 exact and whitespace-collapsed) agrees.
